subject: POC observability: proposed success criteria, dashboards & timeline
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Lena Park <lena@appscale.ai>, Rahul Mehta <rahul.mehta@appscale.ai>
Cc: procurement@appscale.ai
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: POC observability: proposed success criteria & next steps

Hi Lena / Rahul — great discussion today. Quick recap from our discovery and a proposed observability-focused POC plan so we can align on success criteria and owners. Please review and confirm or flag edits.

High-level objective
- Validate that Redwood Inference can meet AppScale AI requirements for predictable latency, cost-per-inference, and model quality observability during a 2-week evaluation with your production-ish workload.

Proposed success criteria (please confirm):
1) Performance: P95 tail latency <= 250ms for the primary /generate route at 95th percentile of observed request patterns during the trial.
2) Reliability: No more than 3 impact-worthy errors (5xx or model fallback) during the trial window.
3) Quality: Model-level BLEU/ROUGE/JointScore measurement on the provided prompt set shows no regression > 3% vs baseline.
4) Observability: Dashboards available showing latency P50/P95/P99, tokens per request, GPU utilization, cache hit ratio, and error classification.
5) Data controls: Logs exported to your S3 bucket (30-day retention) and metrics accessible via Prometheus/Grafana.

POC timeline (proposal)
- May 24–26: infra & network prep (firewalls, VPC peering, bucket access)
- May 27: smoke tests + dashboard baseline
- May 28–Jun 10: evaluation window (2 weeks)
- Jun 11–17: results review & decision

Owners (suggested)
- Redwood: Vanessa Ortiz (primary), Connor O'Brien (SE - observability stack), Rishi Malhotra (security/compliance)
- AppScale: Lena Park (technical), Rahul Mehta (procurement/ops)

Observability asks for your engineering team before kickoff
- Provide an S3 bucket + write creds for log export, or let us push to your BigQuery project.
- Which metrics endpoint do you prefer for Prometheus scraping (IP + port)?
- A short priority prompt set (10–20 prompts) for quality checks.

Attached: AppScale-POC-EvalChecklist.xlsx (draft evaluation checklist)

If this looks good I will loop in Connor & Marissa to draw a concrete dashboard map and test plan. Thanks — Vanessa

--

From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 11:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: POC observability: proposed success criteria & next steps

Vanessa / team — see a concise technical plan / ownership I can deliver on. I kept Lena's 60-day request in mind and proposed trade-offs for retention and cost.

Observability deliverables (POC) — what we'll provide:
1) Dashboards (Grafana)
   - "POC Overview": P50/P95/P99 latency, requests/sec, tokens/sec, error rate, model fallback events
   - "Model Quality": per-prompt pass/fail, rolling drift score, daily aggregate quality delta vs baseline
   - "Infra & Utilization": GPU utilization, memory pressure, batch-size distribution, queue depth, avg batch latency
2) Tracing
   - Jaeger traces for request flows (end-to-end), sampled at 1% by default, adjustable. Span tags include model_id, route, request_size_tokens, worker_id. Retention: keep traces 14 days (compressed storage afterwards).
3) Logs and export
   - Application logs: structured JSON with request_id, model_id, latency_ms, error_code, prompt_hash (PII stripped).
   - Export pipeline: push to their S3 bucket (preferred) with lifecycle rule: hot 60 days -> cold archive. We will also offer an optional filtered copy to their sec team (redacted).
4) Metrics export & access
   - Prometheus metrics endpoint (we can scrape or push a gateway). We will ship a prebuilt dashboard that connects to their Grafana (or spin up a temporary Redwood Grafana read-only view).
5) Alerting & SLOs (recommendations)
   - SLOs: availability 99.9% (errors <= 0.1%), latency SLO: P95 < 250ms.
   - Alerts: P95 breach > 10% sustained for 5m, error rate spike > 0.5% absolute, cache hit ratio < 60%. Alert destinations: PagerDuty + Slack channel.

Retention & cost notes:
- Logs: 60 days hot (as they asked), archive at 61+ days. Metrics: 90 days (high resolution), 1y rollup at lower resolution. Traces: 14 days.

Owners & immediate next steps:
- Connor O'Brien (connor@redwood.com): build Grafana dashboards + Prometheus mapping, run smoke tests (owner for day-0 dashboard).
- Marissa Cole (marissa@redwood.com): trial logistics, runbook, run daily check-ins with AppScale during trial.
- Rishi Malhotra (rishi@redwood.com): validate S3 export permissions, review PII masking approach and compliance notes.

Infra checklist for AppScale (to send to client):
- Create an S3 bucket with write/prefix permissions for service-account redwood-poc@appscale (we'll provide exact ARN).
- Open outbound rules for ports 9090 (Prometheus), 16686 (Jaeger), and 443 for metric push if using gateway.
- Provide a small sample dataset and the 20-prompt validation set.

I can have the dashboard templates and the infra checklist ready by EOD tomorrow.

2) Confirm Prometheus scrape endpoint or open port for push gateway (9090/443)
3) Share 20-prompt validation set and sample production traffic pattern (CSV)
